newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Intel, Morris busy as stocks up.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Intel, Morris busy as stocks up.

text.p: Options on shares of Intel Corp and Philip Morris Cos Inc traded heavily in morning activity as the two stocks rallied sharply.
Traders said that in both cases, option investors were playing the rallies in the stocks.
Marty Kearney at PTI Securities said volatilities on both Intel and Philip Morris calls did not move far from historical levels as the stocks opened higher, then range-traded.
"Some people have been taking profits" in Intel options, one trader said. "But a lot of people are jumping on the bandwagon."
By 1050 CDT (1550 GMT), Intel shares were up 5-5/8 at 94-1/4 on more than 11 million shares. In early trading, the stock reached an all-time high of 94-3/4.
On Monday, the chip maker said its third quarter sales would be better than expected.
The news touched off a round of earnings estimate upgrades by Wall Street analysts.
Among Intel options, most of the action was focused on the October 95 calls, which traded more than 6,700 contracts. The option, which had an open interest of about 2,800, was ahead 2-3/8 at 3-7/8.
The Intel October 90 call traded about 3,450 contracts. It was up 3-5/8 at 6-3/4. Its open interest was 14,186.
The most active put was the September 85, which traded more than 1,600 contracts. It lost 1/4 to 1/16.
Traders said the action in Intel spilled over into other related stocks such as Micron Technology and Atmel Corp .
Among its options, the September 22-1/2 and 25 call each traded more than 800 contracts. The Atmel October 27-1/2 call traded about 3600 contracts.

For Micron Technology, which was active on Monday, the October 25 call was by far the most active, with about 10,300 contracts traded on the Pacific Stock Exchange. On the Chicago Board Options Exchange, the same option traded 2,600.
The option was up 11/16 on both exchanges, trading at three on the Pacific and 2-15/16 on the CBOE.
The corresponding put traded about 3,900 contracts on the Pacific Stock Exchange. On the CBOE, the October 42-1/2 put, down 1-5/8 at 15-1/2, traded 1,500 contracts.
Shares of Philip Morris were boosted by news late Monday that a Florida judge dismissed pre-1994 claims in a Medicaid lawsuit brought against the tobacco industry by the state of Florida.
Philip Morris shares were up 2-1/8 at 94-1/8, off an early session peak of 95.

The Philip Morris September 95 call traded more than 4,600 contraces and was up 7/16 at 9/16. The October 90 call traded about 900 contracts, the October 95 call about 1,000 and the October 100 call roughly 800. --G.Crawford, (312) 408-8750/E-mail: derivatives@reuters.com
